usageNotes: Use this before creating a PVE remote to discover cluster topology and verify connectivity — it returns node addresses and probes each node's TLS so you can confirm whether a fingerprint is required. Requires System.Modify at the root path. If the target PVE uses a self-signed certificate, capture the fingerprint from this response and supply it when calling post_pve_remotes (or the equivalent create endpoint) to avoid TLS verification failures.

examples.summary: Scan a two-node PVE cluster using an API token to pre-populate remote config

tips: The authid format is either 'user@realm' (password auth) or 'user@realm!tokenid' (API token auth); use API token format in automation to avoid embedding passwords.
The response includes all cluster node addresses — use this list to verify every node is reachable before committing the remote config.
If TLS probing returns a fingerprint in the response, store it; subsequent PVE remote operations may require it if the cluster uses a self-signed cert.
This endpoint does not persist any data — it is a read-probe only, safe to call multiple times.
